questions.text: Which of the following correctly defines a set?

questions.text: The cardinality n(A) of a set A means:
options: The number of elements in A
questions.explanation: n(A) is the cardinal number, i.e. the number of elements in A.

questions.text: If A = {2, 4, 6}, then n(A) = ?
questions.explanation: n(A) = 3 because the set contains three elements.

questions.text: The cardinality of {a, b, c, d, e} is:
questions.explanation: The set has five elements.

questions.explanation: A proper subset is not equal to A; A has at least one extra element.

They share at least one element

questions.explanation: A ∪ B = {x : x ∈ A or x ∈ B}.
The union collects all elements of both sets without repetition.

questions.text: The intersection A ∩ B contains:

questions.explanation: A ∩ B = {x : x ∈ A and x ∈ B}.
The only element in both sets is 3.
